meta.title: bottega-kit: you approve the plan, the agents do the rounds
meta.description: Planner, implementer, reviewer and optional judge on Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, Grok Build, Muse Code or the Antigravity CLI. A receipt per dispatch.

hero.lead: A planner writes the plan. You approve it once. Implementer and reviewer take the rounds, up to a cap; a judge says whether to merge. Then a pull request. Every dispatch leaves a receipt.
hero.transcriptCaption: One line per dispatch: the profile, and the model the harness reported.

commands.h2: Six commands. Nothing runs in the background.
commands.lead: A round is one implementer pass and one reviewer pass. The cap is {rounds} unless you change it.

items.what: Worktree, branch, and a `task.md` holding your request verbatim.
One planner dispatch. Answer its questions in `task.md` and plan again.
The gate. Plan hash, roles and cap recorded.
Rounds up to the cap, then the judge. Exit {exitOk} done, {exitStopped} stopped.
Commit if needed, push to origin, open the pull request.
After a stop, with a fresh cap. The only retry.

claims.h2: Made to be *left alone* with a branch.
claims.lead: After approval, nobody asks you anything.

items.title: One gate: the plan.
items.text: Approval records the plan hash. Edit the plan afterwards and `run` refuses, exit {exitRefused}.

items.title: Reviewers review. They do not fix.
items.text: The worktree is hashed before and after every planner, reviewer and judge run. A changed tracked file stops the task.

items.title: No retries. No fallbacks. No model of its own.
items.text: A failed dispatch stops the task; you resume it. A different reported model stops it too.

items.title: Mix vendors, per role.
items.text: Fable plans, Codex builds, GLM reviews on Z.AI's endpoint, without your Anthropic credentials.

loop.h2: After every dispatch, the first rule that matches.

rules.text: The harness failed to start, exited non-zero, reported an error or left no final message: stop.
The reported model is neither the one requested nor an alias: stop.
A planner, reviewer or judge changed a tracked file or HEAD: stop.
The reviewer is next. A commit is a warning, not a stop.
ready: the judge, or done. blocked: stop. needs-work or no signal: the next round, or cap-reached.
ready: done. Anything else: stop, judge-needs-work.

loop.after: Ctrl-C stops a task as interrupted; `bottega resume` continues it.

roles.h2: Four roles. One document between them.
roles.lead: Agents share only `task.md` and report with `bottega signal`. The kit decides from that, never from prose.

items.does: Reads the repository. Writes the plan or asks questions.
Works the to-do items, adds tests, ticks boxes.
items.changes: the worktree and `task.md` boxes; never commits or pushes

items.does: Checks every ticked item, runs the tests and the manual QA.
items.changes: nothing: a changed tracked file stops the task

items.does: Optional. Reads the plan and the diff, says whether to merge.

roles.bindH3: Bind each role to a profile.
roles.bindText: A profile is a harness, a model and an effort. `bottega init` writes this starter when it finds `claude` and `codex`. Fable plans and judges, Opus builds and reviews. A Claude profile on another endpoint runs with {proxyStripped} Anthropic variables removed.

harnesses.h2: Six harnesses, the narrowest permissions each offers.
harnesses.lead: Every flag in one table, pinned by a test. Shown: the implementer's command.
harnesses.claude: Claude Code, headless. Read tools only for the planner; `git push` and `gh` denied to the implementer and reviewer.
harnesses.codex: Codex CLI, `exec`. Read-only sandbox for the planner, workspace-write for the rest; network blocked by default. No model is reported, so the receipt says requested-only.
harnesses.kimi: Kimi Code, `-p`. An agent file gives each role its tools; `git push` to origin and `gh` fail through the environment. No model is reported, so the receipt says requested-only and keeps the tokens from the session log.
harnesses.after: Before each release a live run replaces the verified snapshot.
harnesses.grok: Grok Build, headless. Each role gets its tool list and allow and deny rules; Claude Code's and Cursor's configuration stays out. The model is reported and checked, the cost recorded.
harnesses.muse: Muse Code, `exec`. No writes or shell for the planner, no writes for the reviewer and judge; contributor mode off for every dispatch. The models Muse Code names are checked.
harnesses.agy: Antigravity CLI, `-p`. Each dispatch runs with a temporary HOME holding the role's permission rules and a link to your sign-in; your own settings, hooks and MCP servers stay out. No model is reported, so the receipt says requested-only.

receipt.text: One directory per dispatch, outside the repository, so it outlives the worktree. Variable names, never values. MIT; you pay your providers.

items.what: requested and reported model, argv, timings, usage, cost
on failure: phase, reason, last stderr lines
what the agent signalled, and when

install.text: You need git, gh, python3 3.9 or newer, and one of `claude`, `codex`, `kimi`, `grok`, `muse` or `agy`, logged in. bottega-kit never handles their credentials. `init` writes a starter; `doctor` checks it.
